title: Structured Output Certification & Enterprise Intake Triage
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Summary: Define a lightweight, repeatable intake and certification path for enterprise Hosted API requests that require structured outputs (JSON/CSV/protobuf-like schemas), plus a priority scorer to triage requests for fast-path onboarding. Goal is to reduce back-and-forth with customers, avoid production regressions from unvalidated schema assumptions, and give engineering clear signal-driven SLAs for rollout.

Why this exists: Enterprise customers frequently request schema-locked outputs (e.g., machine-readable invoices, clinical notes, legal clause extraction) with strong reliability and deterministic shapes. Current intake is ad-hoc: PMs collect examples, engs do manual validation, and runtime teams handle fallbacks case-by-case. This causes long onboarding times, bursty engineering work, and production incidents when schema drift occurs. A certification rubric + priority scorer should standardize expectations and speed up safe delivery.

Scope: Design the certification template (schema spec, validation tests, acceptance criteria), the priority scoring heuristic (signals and weights), and a minimal tooling checklist for PM/RSE/SE/Docs. Work with Runtime, SDK, and Design to produce: a Confluence intake template, an example GitHub PR template with test fixtures, an automated schema check harness for CI, and a monitoring playbook to detect schema regressions post-launch.

Out-of-scope: Full production SDK changes to enforce schemas in all languages (this work will be a follow-on), heavy-weight per-customer contract negotiations, and private deployment packaging (except for documenting special-case requirements).
acceptance_criteria: Confluence intake template created with: required fields (schema example, validation dataset, expected failure modes, latency/cost SLO target, fallback behavior)
Priority scorer documented with clear signal definitions and scoring thresholds (auto-low, needs-se-signal, fast-path) and an example mapping for high-risk enterprise customers
A sample GitHub PR in the runtime repo that wires a schema validation test using a small fixture set (pass/fail) and an example CI check
Rollout checklist with staging verification steps, rollout gating signals (schema-mismatch-rate < 0.1% over 1h, tokens-per-request within expected bounds), and rollback criteria
Post-launch monitoring dashboard proto (errors-by-schema, mismatch-trend, latency-by-schema) linked in the playbook
updates: 2026-03-06: Kickoff with PM, Runtime, SDK, and SE teams. Agreed scope: intake template + priority scorer + CI test harness prototype.

2026-03-08: Runtime team (Leads: Samuel Ortiz) flagged two constraints: (1) schema enforcement at tokenization boundaries is non-trivial for incremental streaming; (2) current KV-cache optimizations assume opaque string outputs for some models. We noted these as technical risks and added a dependency on ENG-18873 for streaming-compatible schema checks.

2026-03-09: Draft intake template uploaded to Confluence: link https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Structured+Output+Intake (internal). Added required attachments: canonical schema example, minimal validation set, fallback contract section.

2026-03-10: Prototype CI test created in https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime PR#4567. The test runs 50 sample generations against the schema and asserts shape/field types. Runtime team suggested adding tokenization-aware post-process checks for streaming clients.

2026-03-12: PM/Design review: added UX guidance for API error responses (machine-readable error codes for schema violations) and a recommended ‘soft-fail’ flag for first 2 weeks of rollout to avoid hard outages during customer onboarding. Decided to include a migration note for legacy customers that cannot adopt strict schemas immediately.
decisions: Adopt a two-track certification: 'Strict' (schema enforcement with CI gating) and 'Guided' (schema validation + soft-fail logs, delayed enforcement).
Priority scorer will be primarily signal-driven (customer tier, request complexity, expected tokens/second, security/compliance needs) with a manual override path for SE-team escalations.
Streaming clients will use post-hoc validation of assembled output and a 'soft-fail' grace window for first 72 hours of production traffic.
Do not block initial certification on full SDK enforcement in all languages; provide server-side and JS/py snippets as reference implementations instead.
attachments: GitHub: runtime PR#4567 - prototype schema CI test - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567
notes_for_engineering: Runtime should provide a lightweight validation hook that takes final assembled output and a declarative JSON schema; for streaming, provide optional incremental sanity checks (field prefix checks). Work with Runtime to instrument mismatch metrics (per-tenant) so priority scorer can rely on historical stability.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: onboard 2 engineering tenants to validate template and CI tests (1 week)
2) Beta: invite 3 enterprise customers (with SE support) to run through certification (2 weeks)
3) Monitor: collect schema-mismatch rate, latency delta, and false-positive rate for soft-fail; target mismatch < 0.1% before strict enforcement
4) Enforce: flip to strict enforcement for new tenants once signals are green; provide migration paths for legacy tenants
